senses.gloss:
Tuṣa, in the Atharvaveda^1 and later,^2 regularly denotes the
‘husk’ of grain, often used for a fire.^3
1) ix. 6, 16; xi. 1, 12, 29; 3, 5; xii. 3,
19.
2) Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 5, 5;
Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, ii. 7, 9, etc.
3) Tuṣa-pakva, Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 2,
4, 2; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 2, 4;
Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, vii. 2, 1, 7.

Tūṣa is found in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas^1
denoting the ‘fringe’ or ‘trimming’ of a garment.
1) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, i. 8, 1, 1; ii. 4,
9, 1; vi. 1, 1, 3; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā,
xxiii. 1; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 6,
1, 8; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, xvii. 1,
etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 262.
